name: AnySkin (research sensor)

sources.title: R. Bhirangi, V. Pattabiraman, E. Erciyes, Y. Cao, T. Hellebrekers and L. Pinto, "AnySkin: Plug-and-play Skin Sensing for Robotic Touch", arXiv:2409.08276
sources.covers: sensing principle (magnetised elastomer over 5 magnetometers, the ReSkin circuitry), skin thickness 2 mm, triangular fingertip shape, self-adhering skin, data collection rate 100 Hz in the experiments, signal strength and variability (Table I), replacement time (Table II)

note: A contact sensor, modelled by pad coverage, not a workspace camera, so it has no imagers. A research magnetic skin (open source): a magnetised elastomer (particles in Dragonskin 10 Slow) over "the same 5-magnetometer circuitry as ReSkin", self-adhering, replaceable in about 12 s. Figures from the paper: skin thickness 2 mm; the experiments' fingertip skin is triangular (its size is not stated, so pad_mm is null; the 20 mm x 20 mm skin in the alignment test is a ReSkin-style comparison skin); tactile data collected at 100 Hz in the policy experiments (entered as fps; the sensor's maximum rate is not stated). taxels is null: the 5 magnetometers (3-axis each) are not taxels in the sense of a pad grid. Not stated: power, mass, size, interface (the ReSkin electronics use a microcontroller board). Its readings are not an image stream, so no stream is entered; the bandwidth budget needs the data rate as a measured or stated figure.
